title: EmbeddingGemma 2 Expands Beyond Text to Support Code, Images, Video, and Audio
gist: Google released EmbeddingGemma 2, an Apache 2.0 open-weight model built on Gemma 4 that embeds text, code, images, video and audio into one 768-dimensional space, scaling from 270M to 740M parameters for on-device use. MRL truncation cuts storage sixfold but costs retrieval quality, especially for non-text modalities.

insights.claim: EmbeddingGemma 2 is a compact open-weight multimodal embedding model based on Gemma 4 under Apache 2.0, aimed at efficient on-device semantic search and RAG.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Permissive licensing and small size make local multimodal retrieval a commodity capability.
insights.quote: Based on Gemma 4 and released under the Apache 2.0 license

insights.claim: The model represents text, code, images, video and audio in a single 768-dimensional embedding space, so developers can search across media types without maintaining separate incompatible embedding spaces.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Unified spaces simplify retrieval architecture and reduce index infrastructure for multimodal apps.
insights.quote: represent text, code, images, video, and audio in a unified 768-dimensional embedding space

insights.claim: Developers can load only the encoders they need, ranging from 270 million parameters for text and code to 740 million for full multimodal support.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Modular footprints fit consumer hardware like phones and laptops.
insights.quote: scaling from 270 million parameters for text and code to 740 million for full multimodal support
insights.locator: The model allows developers to load only

insights.claim: Google says EmbeddingGemma 2 significantly outperforms EmbeddingGemma 1 on code search and technical retrieval, making it suited to local codebase indexing and agentic code search.
insights.speaker: Google
insights.so_what: Local code indexing is a growing use case tied to coding agents and privacy needs.
insights.quote: significantly outperforms EmbeddingGemma 1 on code search and technical retrieval

insights.claim: The first EmbeddingGemma targeted offline and privacy-sensitive scenarios such as local personal-file search and mobile RAG pipelines with Gemma 3n.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Edge and privacy-first retrieval is a consistent product strategy for Google's open models.

insights.claim: Matryoshka truncation lets 768-dimension vectors shrink to 128 dimensions, cutting storage for a million bfloat16 vectors from about 1.5 GB to 250 MB, a sixfold reduction.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Cheap vector storage lowers cost of large on-device or cloud indexes.
insights.quote: takes roughly 1.5 GB of memory, while truncating them to 128 dimensions requires just 250 MB

insights.claim: At 128 dimensions the model retains about 90% of quality for text but only around 75% for image, video and speech retrieval, so Google recommends truncating only when storage or speed require it.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Truncation penalties are modality-dependent, so multimodal indexes should not be compressed as aggressively as text.
insights.quote: performance drops to around 75% for image, video, and speech retrieval

insights.claim: A commenter argues the notable advance is shared semantic space for images and audio, while text-only gains are not a massive improvement.
insights.speaker: Distinct-Target7503
insights.so_what: Value of upgrading depends on whether a workload is multimodal.
insights.quote: for text only it is not a massive improvement

insights.claim: Practitioners warn that task prefixes are not optional and that for MRL one should slice first and then L2-normalize, since normalizing at 768 and then cutting gives off-norm vectors.
insights.speaker: Open-Adhesiveness-86
insights.so_what: Implementation mistakes can silently hurt recall, so correct prefixing and normalization order matter for production RAG.
insights.quote: slice first then L2-normalize the shorter vector
